description: ABI Coverage Grid manifest — the single source of truth for thin-corner runtime coverage cells. See src/docs/Design/abi-coverage-grid.md. Phase 1 enumerates the closure / inout / tuple corners as a full cross-product and grades each cell on every declared+exercised runtime (sim = Mono JIT, device = NativeAOT). Phase 2 adds the GENERICS corner (generics.*): the CSM (ConcreteSpecializationEngine) method-level constraint specialization path (inline + where-clause protocol composition, struct/class conformers) and the open-generic constrained FREE-function CallConvSwift [Obsolete(SB0001)] fallback path (single constraint, composition, multi-where, two-type-param where-clause), plus two by-design-gray boundaries — a Self-requirement constraint (sumTwo) and the async closure-param fan-out leg. Cells map to tests by (class, method) name over the existing test-results JSONL + TestClasses.g.txt inventory; rename-rot (a cite absent from the inventory) is a hard integrity error. Disposition: expect-green (release-gating), supported-low-priority (reported, not gated), by-design-gray (intentionally unsupported, cites a roadmap rationale). DOCUMENTED ABSENCES (deliberately out of slice-1 scope, recorded here per design §5 rather than silently dropped): nested tuple returns ((A,B),C) — no fixture authored; sync tuple returns with a generic element (only the async-on-generic-parent shape exists, and it is suppressed by design — see tuple.ret.pair.contains-generic.async); async-closure-PARAM fan-out (NOW FOLDED IN as generics.closure-fanout.async.closure-param.{peer,owner}: the sync closure-PARAM/closure-RETURN legs are closure.fanout.same-signature.* and the async leg is by-design-gray — its conformance compiles after the owner-selection + branch-filter fix, but async closure-param reverse dispatch is compile-gated only, so its runtime fixtures are [Skip]); non-void closure RETURN (the closure-returning materialiser — IsDispatchableClosureReturningMethod — dispatches only a zero-arg `() -> Void` returned closure; a non-void returned closure like `() -> Int32` falls to the fatalError stub and is an unimplemented capability, orthogonal to the fan-out Latent, so the closure-RETURN fan-out cells use the supported `() -> Void` shape with a C#-side side-effect oracle); the full closure direction×escaping×effects×arity cross-product (the basics are already covered by existing ClosureTests/ClosureEdgeCaseTests and represented below; only the Latent-tied fan-out leg is newly authored).

cells.reason: HasInoutWithAbiMismatch rejects non-frozen (resilient) struct inout: a resilient struct is read through a pointer (no fixed layout), so it cannot be marshalled as a blittable `ref T` stack buffer with write-back. The method is not emitted — there is no runtime surface by design. Architectural ABI limitation, same family as the inout ObjC-bridgeable rejection (roadmap: 'Inout ObjC-bridgeable reverse-dispatch keeps a dead vtable slot').

inout ObjC-bridgeable (URL/URLRequest/Decimal) is rejected by HasInoutWithAbiMismatch on the direct path (the {p}Ref/{p}Copy write-back mismatch does not compile) and routed to a fatalError trap stub on the reverse-dispatch path. Roadmap 'Inout ObjC-bridgeable reverse-dispatch keeps a dead vtable slot' deferred it as disproportionate to a cosmetic dead slot on a near-unreachable signature; no active repro. No consumable runtime surface by design.

cells.reason: A sync/async tuple return with a generic element on a generic-parent extension (AsyncGenericContainer<T>.fetchPair() async -> (T, Int32)) is intentionally suppressed by the generator: a @_silgen_name async wrapper on a generic-parent extension is a generic instance method that expects self + parent type metadata in implicit registers, while a fixed CallConvSwift P/Invoke can only pass them as trailing IntPtr args — an ABI mismatch that SIGSEGVs. The 'properly suppressed' invariant is asserted in Swift.Bindings.Unit.Tests (MemberValidationPipelineTests.ValidateMethodEmission_AsyncOnGenericParent_*). No runtime surface by design; the correct long-term fix is a generic-static-dispatch @_cdecl async bridge.

cells.reason: An open-generic free function constrained on a Self-requirement protocol — sumTwo<T: Summable>(_:_:) -> T where Summable is `func add(_ other: Self) -> Self` — is uncallable from C# by any generated path. A Self-requirement protocol projects its C# interface with Self erased to Swift.AnyType (ISummable carries `Swift.AnyType Add(Swift.AnyType)`), and NO value-type conformer is emitted as `: ISummable` (the witness table is registered for Swift-internal/existential use only — the same boundary roadmap/constraints record as 'PAT and Self-requirement protocols ARE rejected for existential params'). The open-generic SumTwo<T> where T : ISummable therefore has no satisfying C# argument. This is a by-design boundary of Self-requirement constraints, not a fixable round-trip cell; no fixture by design. Long-term lift would require materializing a concrete Self-typed conformer surface, out of scope.

ASYNC closure-PARAM same-signature fan-out, PEER leg: AsyncClosureFanOwner/AsyncClosureFanPeer both declare `applyFactory(_: @escaping () -> Int32) async`. The EveryProtocol owner/peer grouping is async-INSENSITIVE (GetSwiftMethodFullSignature drops async), so these share a fan-out group with the sync ClosureFan{Owner,Peer} declaring the same selector. ComputeMethodEmissionPlans owner-selection hands the witness BODY to the sync, non-throwing sibling (so the group conforms and the sync legs dispatch correctly), and the closure fan-out branch list is filtered to siblings that emit a vtable func field — an async closure-param method has none (IsDispatchableAsyncClosureMethod bails on method.IsAsync; its per-protocol vtable carries only csVTHandle). The async conformance + @_cdecl wrappers COMPILE (this is what the fixture gates, without regressing the sync fan-out), but the shared sync witness reads the SYNC vtables; an async proxy registers an async receiver thunk whose result is a Task, so reached through the sync @convention(c) pointer it would return garbage. Async closure-param REVERSE dispatch is therefore compile-gated only; the runtime fixtures are [Skip]. Long-term lift needs the Task-bridging machinery the dispatchable-async-closure gate (IsDispatchableAsyncClosureParam, restricted to `() async -> Int32` PARAMS) does not yet extend to async METHODS — out of scope.

OWNER leg of the async closure-param fan-out — same rationale as generics.closure-fanout.async.closure-param.peer: the shared sync witness cannot route an async receiver thunk's Task result through the sync @convention(c) pointer, so async closure-param reverse dispatch is compile-gated only and the runtime fixture is [Skip]. The fixture gates that the async conformance compiles without regressing the sync fan-out.

cells.runtimeNote: CONSUMER-DIRECTION (C#-construction) round-trip on a generic enum with a nested type on the generic outer: C# builds `VerificationOutcome<SwiftString>.Failure.Expired` and hands it INTO Swift via MakeUnverifiedOutcomeString (param leg, C#->Swift), then destructures the returned `.unverified(String, Failure)` outer case (return leg, Swift->C#). Guards the nested-type-on-generic-outer emission fix (the nested `Failure` subtracts ancestor-inherited generic params so it declares no own params; previously CS0693/CS0305). This is the inverted direction the symbol/arity/vtable parity gates do not assert — they cover Swift->C# artifact emission, not a C#-built generic-enum case crossing back in. Both runtimes: tuple-payload marshalling + generic-enum metadata differ between Mono JIT (sim) and NativeAOT (device).

Return-leg detail of the same C#-construction round-trip: asserts TryGetUnverified destructures the `.unverified` payload tuple positionally — element 0 the String payload, element 1 the nested `Failure.Expired` case. Exercises mixed-payload (String + nested-enum) tuple extraction from a generic enum back into C#. Both runtimes for the same tuple-marshalling/metadata reason.

Breadth leg: C# constructs each nested `Failure` case (Expired/Malformed/NotAuthorized) and round-trips it through Swift, asserting the case tag and String payload survive both directions for every case. Proves the nested-case C#-construction surface is complete, not just the first case. Both runtimes.

Payload-size leg: a 64 KiB String payload round-trips through the C#-constructed generic-enum factory, guarding the SBW_Utf8Slice bridge against truncation/boundary bugs on a large associated value carried inside a generic enum. Both runtimes.

The non-failure sibling case: C# round-trips the `.verified(String)` case (MakeVerifiedOutcomeString) and asserts TryGetVerified yields the payload while TryGetUnverified correctly returns false on a Verified value. Confirms the nested-type fix did not regress the outer enum's other case. Both runtimes.
